questions.q: Why does Mara choose an Azure Automation Runbook with a managed identity over a cron job with a stored credential?
options: Runbooks are the only option that supports Python

A system-assigned managed identity lets the runbook authenticate to Graph and Azure Resource Manager with no stored secret at all, removing exactly the kind of standing credential this capstone has been trying to eliminate
Cron jobs cannot run on a daily schedule
Runbooks are free while cron jobs cost money
questions.explain: A managed identity eliminates the stored credential a cron job would otherwise need, which is consistent with this capstone's broader push away from long-lived, standing credentials.

questions.q: In the test case, what happens when the SCADA-Emergency-Access policy is attached directly to the test account svc-scada-test-01, without adding it to the scada-ot-admins group?
options: The script fails to run at all
The script should show svc-scada-test-01 with access_path: "direct_assignment", proving the script catches access a group-membership-only review would miss
The test account is automatically added to the group
Nothing changes in the script's output, since group membership is required for any account to appear
questions.explain: This is the test that matters most: it directly proves the script surfaces a non-group-based grant with access_path set to "direct_assignment" before that capability is relied on for a real finding.

questions.q: Why does the test case run the script a second time with no changes in between?
options: To check that the script runs faster the second time
To validate idempotency — the same unchanged input should produce identical output both times, which is what makes a daily unattended schedule trustworthy
To test whether the script can be run twice without crashing the server
There is no second run in the test case
questions.explain: Confirming identical output on a repeat run with no underlying change validates idempotency, which matters because a non-idempotent script would produce false-looking changes on a daily schedule.

questions.q: Why is the runbook's managed identity scoped read-only (Security Reader / Reader) rather than given write access?
options: Write access was requested but denied due to licensing limits
The script's job is to report on access, not change it, so granting write permissions would needlessly widen its own blast radius
Read-only identities run faster than write-capable ones
Azure Automation does not support write-capable managed identities
questions.explain: Since the script only inventories access, a read-only scope avoids giving the automation itself any unnecessary ability to modify access — minimizing its own blast radius.

questions.q: What does a successful, scheduled production run of this script set up for the rest of the capstone?
options: Nothing further — this closes out the capstone entirely
It gives ScadaAccessInventory_CL a current, queryable daily refresh, which becomes direct input to the GRC risk register and is about to be checked against a separate compliance audit's own count
It automatically generates the board presentation slides
It replaces the need for the network segmentation work from earlier lessons
questions.explain: The now-running inventory feeds Lesson 10's risk register and will be compared, independently, against the compliance audit's count starting in Lesson 11 — where this capstone's central discrepancy begins.
